newsitem.title: USA: PP&L seeks customer choice pilot approval.
newsitem.headline: PP&L seeks customer choice pilot approval.

text.p: Pennsylvania Power & Light Co said on Tuesday that it is seeking state Public Utility Commission approval by April 1 of its proposed pilot test of customer choice of electricity suppliers.
The PP&L Resources Inc subsidiary said its program would provide more than 54,000 customers with an opportunity to choose their electricity supplier as early as next summer.
Calling itself the first state utility to file a customer choice pilot program, PP&L said its customers could begin selecting their electricity supplier in July if the commission approves.
"PP&L is calling on all Pennsylvania utilities to propose similar pilots to ensure that customers statewide have real choices," chief executive William F. Hecht said.

"The program we are filing today is a significant information-gathering component of the effort to provide all customers with the opportunity to select their electricity supplier. We continue to believe that it is possible to have a fully competitive electricity marketplace by the end of this decade -- or sooner," said Hecht.
He said PP&L designed its pilot to test limited elements of a more competitive electricity marketplace -- mainly the process of customers' selection of an electricity supplier.

If the proposal is approved, beginning in April PP&L will recruit customers to participate in the program. About 5 percent of the company's customers will have the opportunity to pick the company that generates their electricity.

PP&L said it will also notify outside generation suppliers of the opportunity to participate in the pilot. Transmission and delivery of the electricity to customers' homes will continue to be provided by PP&L.
Specifically, PP&L said, the program it filed with the commission seeks to:
-- Give about 48,000 residential customers the opportunity to participate, along with about 6,000 of its commercial and industrial customers.
-- Have commission approve suppliers participating in the pilot.
-- Allow other utilities to offer electricity to PP&L customers if those utilities allow PP&L to offer electricity to their customers.
If more customers volunteer than can be accommodated, PP&L said, those to participate in the pilot will be selected at random.
To permit "shopping" during the pilot program, PP&L will offer about a $0.02 per kilowatt-hour credit to customers.
If a supplier is offering electricity at less than $0.02 per kilowatt-hour, the customer can save money.
PP&L said it "is convinced that electricity will be available at less than $0.02 per kilowatt-hour."
